sentences.text: MFA No.11254/2011 is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation.
3. The brief facts of the case are that the deceased Siddegowda was working under respondent No.1 as coolie.

On 23.12.2005, he was proceeding in a tractor and trailer bearing No.KA-13-T-4963-4964 to load raagi grass into the tractor and trailer, which is owned by respondent No.1, when the tractor and trailer reached near Huragalawaadi Village, the driver of the tractor and trailer drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, due to which, the tractor and trailer turtled.
Due to the impact, the deceased Siddegowda succumbed to the injuries.
Therefore, the claimants preferred claim petition seeking compensation.

4. Learned Commissioner has awarded compensation by fixing liability on the Insurance Company holding that the relationship of employer and employee proved between respondent - H.T.Mohan Kumar and the deceased respectively.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company submitted that in the present case, the relationship of employer and employee is not proved between the H.T.Mohan Kumar and the deceased.
Therefore, learned Commissioner has committed an error in appreciating the evidence on record.
He places reliance on Ex.P1-Complaint, FIR, Ex.R3 & R4 - the judgments rendered in MVC No.2132/2006 dated 13.06.2009 and MVC No.2133/2006 dated 02.07.2008 by the MACT.

Also referred to the evidence rendered by the complainant- Eranna before learned Commissioner/
MACT.
Therefore, it is submitted that the claimants have failed to proved that the respondent -H.T.Mohan Kumar is employer of the deceased.

Further, it is submitted that just because the charge sheet is filed that it is not a gospel truth and in the motor vehicle cases before the MACT, it was held that the Tractor was taken on hire basis.
Hence, the liability is to be fixed on the respondent- H.T.Mohan Kumar being the owner of the tractor and trailer on the ground that the said vehicle was taken on hire basis.
Therefore, it is submitted that there is no relationship of employer and employee between the respondent -H.T.Mohan Kumar and the deceased.

6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimants submitted that even though initially in the complaint, it is stated that the tractor and trailer was taken on hire basis for loading raagi grass but it was stated in a fear of anxiety, but later, he has clarified that the deceased had worked as coolie employee under the employment of respondent- H.T.Mohan Kumar and resultantly, the charge sheet is filed stating that the deceased had worked as coolie under the employment of the respondent - H.T.Mohan Kumar.

Therefore, it is submitted that the learned Commissioner has Smt. Lakshmamma vs The Branch Manager on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114533109/
4 rightly appreciated the evidence on record by holding relationship between the employer and employee is proved and accordingly, granted compensation by fixing liability on the Insurance Company since the insurance policy is farmer's package policy.

sentences.text: 7. The claimant application under Employee's Compensation Act is to be considered or in other words, it can be said it is maintainable only when the relationship of employer and employee is proved, otherwise not.
In this regard, Ex.P1 - complaint/FIR is to be considered.

Soon after the accident, the said complaint was filed by one Eranna, who is also stated to be traveling in the tractor and trailer that tractor and trailer No.KA-13-T-4963-4964 was taken on hire basis from one H.T.Mohan Kumar for loading raagi grass from their fields.

Therefore, at very initial point of time, it is stated that the complainant - Eranna, Ramesh and the deceased - Siddegowda has taken the said tractor and trailer on hire basis for loading raagi grass from their fields.

Subsequently, the said complainant - Eranna had given further statements by modifying his earlier statement that the deceased has worked as a coolie for loading the raagi grass on the tractor and trailer.
Although in the said further statement, there is no statement that the deceased was working as the employee under the employment of the respondent- H.T.Mohan Kumar.
The charge sheet is filed to the effect that when the deceased was working as coolie for loading raagi grass and while traveling in the said tractor, the accident was caused and the deceased died.
Although in the charge sheet, it is not mentioned that the deceased was working as employee under the employment of the respondent - H.T.Mohan Kumar.

Further, learned counsel for the Insurance Company relied on the Exs.R3 & R4 which are judgments and awards delivered in MVC No.2132/2006 dated 13.06.2009 and MVC No.2133/2006 dated 02.07.2008 that the MACT has observed since tractor was taken on hire basis.
Hence, violation of condition of insurance policy.
Hence, the liability fixed on the owner - H.T.Mohan Kumar.
Therefore, upon considering all these evidences on record, the claimants have not produced evidence to prove that H.T.Mohan Kumar was employer of the deceased.

Just because,
the owner - H.T.Mohan Kumar had filed written statement claiming to be the employer of the deceased that is not sufficient.
When comparing this statement of the owner - H.T.Mohan Kumar with the complaint lodged by the Eranna at an initial point of time, it is stated that the tractor and trailer was taken on hire basis.
Therefore, there is contra material in this regard.
Furthermore, the said respondent - H.T.Mohan Kumar had not appeared - 10 - before the Court for tendering his evidence.

Had the said owner- H.T.Mohan Kumar entered witness box, then the Insurance Company would have got an opportunity to cross-examine the said H.T.Mohan Kumar then it may be revealed whether H.T.Mohan Kumar is the employer or not of the deceased.

Therefore, even though the claimants have stated that the respondent - H.T.Mohan Kumar was the employer of the deceased and also said that H.T.Mohan Kumar had filed a written statement stating that he was the employer of the deceased, the complaint states that the tractor was taken on a hire basis.

Therefore, in order to give one more opportunity to the claimants to prove that the deceased was an employee under the respondent - H.T.Mohan Kumar, the matter is required to be remanded to the Tribunal for fresh consideration regarding aspect of relationship of employer and employee between the respondent - H.T.Mohan Kumar and deceased - Siddegowda.

Just because, the respondent - H.T.Mohan Kumar had filed a written statement is not sufficient and also Smt. Lakshmamma vs The Branch Manager on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114533109/

The Insurance Company also needs to be given an opportunity to cross- examine the said H.T.Mohan Kumar in case said Mohan Kumar enters into the witness box.
8. Therefore, the matter is required to be remanded to the Tribunal for fresh consideration on adjudication of employer-employee relationship as observed above.

9. Further, whatever observations are made as above stated are only for the purpose of assigning the reasons for remanding the matter to the Tribunal and the same shall not be construed as observation on merits.
Therefore, only for the purpose of assigning reasons for remand, the above said observations are made.
10. The contentions of all the parties are left open.
The parties are directed to appear before the Tribunal on 27.04.2023, without expecting further Notice in this - 12 - regard, and shall adduce any further evidence, if they are so advised.

Accordingly, I pass the following :
ORDER i. MFA No.7956/2011 filed by the Insurance Company is Allowed.
The impugned judgment and award 19.04.2011, passed in KPK/F/SR/No.90 of 2007, on the file of the Labour Officer And Commissioner for Workmen Compensation Sub-Division, Hassan is Set-Aside.
The matter is Remanded to the Tribunal.
ii. MFA No.11254/2011 filed by the claimant seeking enhancement does not survive for consideration for the present.
Therefore, the appeal filed by the claimant is liable to be Disposed off for the present.

The parties are directed to appear before the Tribunal on 27.04.2023, without expecting further Notice in this regard, and shall adduce any further evidence, if they are so advised.
iv.
The amount in deposit shall be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.
v. Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
vi. No order as to costs.
